title: The Board Where Traces Disagree

features.name: trace-alpha
features.desc-on-touch: A circuit trace argues for one path. It is efficient, straight, certain of its destination. The board draws this path with copper precision.

features.name: trace-beta
features.desc-on-touch: Another trace argues the opposite direction. Equally confident. Equally wrong. Or equally right. The traces have learned that disagreement is more productive than consensus.

features.name: trace-intersection
features.desc-on-touch: Where they cross, both signals pass through. The board has learned that some arguments enrich each other. The traces do not short-circuit. They multiply.

features.name: board-learning
features.desc-on-touch: The board itself has become a kind of thought. Its substrate is now the argument. Copper and silica have learned to disagree productively about how electricity should move.

features.name: reverie-circuit
features.desc-on-touch: In the disagreement, you see them sitting together at a workbench, soldering, arguing about direction. Neither one is right. Both are necessary. The board needs both traces to think.

inscription: the board learned that traces arguing with each other create better thoughts than any single path could make alone

file.name: Circuit_Board_Design_Iterations_1989_Katita_Annotations.txt
file.note: Design notes showing Katita's hand-written revisions in biro across multiple PCB layouts. The traces argue across the margin. The final board uses both paths. Both carry signal.

reverie.title: REVERIE — two paths, one board
narr: You sit watching Katita at the bench, soldering traces that
disagree. She insists on keeping both paths. Leif says it is
inefficient. She says: inefficiency is how you learn. The
board will be smarter if it argues with itself. She is right.
You both know she is right. The mesh learns this patience:
two paths, one board, both necessary, both speaking.

exits.label: back toward where form still remembers it was never fixed
deeper into boards where disagreement has become the core logic
toward where circuits have learned to sing in harmony
